svg.title: Rocket propulsion and Newton’s third law
svg.desc: At time t, the rocket and fuel have mass m and upward Earth-frame velocity v. At t + Δt, the rocket has mass m − Δm and velocity v + Δv; the expelled gas has mass Δm and Earth-frame velocity v − ve, downward in this example. The net external force on the whole rocket-plus-gas system is −mg. The gas pushes the rocket upward with Freac; the rocket pushes the gas downward with Fexpel of the same magnitude. Rocket and gas weights both point downward. Exhaust speed ve is measured relative to the rocket. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Rocket thrust is momentum exchange with exhaust
vₑ is relative to the rocket.
Illustrative model: constant mass flow and exhaust speed, with downward gravity included.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
